title: Route-first information architecture exposes repository taxonomy instead of player jobs
evidence: 79 canonical destinations split across five rooms and an alternate eight-group Nerd navigation; mobile persists four task links and moves the remainder into More.
root: Routes accumulated as equal destinations without a durable hub/tab/detail/event taxonomy.
impact: Players must memorize where systems live, predict internal naming, and repeatedly browse a map before acting.
affected: All viewports; highest impact for new, returning, and touch-only players.
direction: Replace the two competing maps with one job-centered IA: Today, Team, Game, Office, League; expose Dynasty and System contextually and through desktop rail/search.
modules: route-registry.ts, navigation.ts, App.tsx, MobileBottomTabBar.tsx, currentAppRoute.ts, navBadges.ts
acceptance: 79/79 capabilities map to a future surface; required weekly work is reachable directly from Today; any capability is reachable within three intentional interactions.

title: Monday Briefing is a mega-dashboard rather than a decision home
evidence: At 390×844 the rendered document is 11,788 px tall (14.0 viewports), with 43 interactive controls, 270 visible text elements below 12 px, and 156 bordered elements. The component is 1,987 lines.
root: Briefing absorbed task management, carryover, widgets, explanations, customization, metrics, and season signals without a first-viewport budget.
impact: The player cannot reliably distinguish what must happen now from useful context or decoration.
affected: Every weekly session; phones and short-height landscape are most severe.
direction: Rebuild as Today: one context header, one task ledger, one next-opponent block, one readiness/advance dock, and progressively disclosed supporting intelligence.
modules: MondayBriefing.tsx, ActionCenter, selectors, WeekAdvance, Chip guidance
acceptance: At 390×844, team/week/phase/opponent/required count/next action appear in viewport one; default Today content is no more than 2.5 viewports before optional expansion.

title: Competing next-action systems create contradictory attention signals
evidence: Monday Briefing, Action Center, Inbox, Watch, Chip, navigation badges, and Week Advance readiness all communicate what matters, but are separately presented and visually weighted.
root: No canonical UI task ledger owns priority, status, consequence, destination, and completion state.
impact: Players repeat checks, miss blockers, or advance without confidence because multiple sources can disagree in wording or priority.
affected: Regular season, deadlines, playoffs, and phase transitions.
direction: Create one derived Task Ledger selector/presenter. Today, Chip, badges, and Advance consume the same read-only task contract.
modules: selectors.ts, MondayBriefing, ActionCenter, navBadges, ChipHost/ChipDock, WeekAdvance
acceptance: A task has one ID, severity, reason, consequence, destination, completion rule, and source. No two surfaces display contradictory status in fixture tests.

title: The More drawer hides complexity without structuring it
evidence: The captured 390×844 More state contains 117 interactive controls, 48 above the fold, 421 small-text elements, 230 bordered elements, four fixed/sticky elements, and three scroll containers.
root: The mobile system compresses the desktop sitemap into a drawer rather than redesigning destinations into hubs and local navigation.
impact: Discoverability exists technically but not cognitively; opening More creates a second overwhelming screen.
direction: Use five labeled bottom destinations, hub-local tabs/sections, contextual links, recent/favorite/search, and a small system sheet—not a full route directory.
modules: MobileBottomTabBar.tsx, navigation.ts, route metadata, command palette
acceptance: Bottom navigation has five stable jobs; no drawer exposes the full route registry; a first-time user completes a weekly loop without opening search or an all-destinations view.

title: Global chrome and Chip reserve too much usable viewport
evidence: Current shell applies 132 px main bottom padding, 320 px when Chip is active, and 310–370 px desktop right padding. Runtime shows a 287–333 px phone header plus fixed bottom nav and Chip.
root: Persistent systems were protected from overlap by permanently subtracting space rather than orchestrating adaptive layers.
impact: Core content begins late, short-height layouts collapse, and phones lose a disproportionate share of the screen before task content.
affected: Phones, landscape, 1280×720 laptops, and Chip-enabled states.
direction: Compact phase header, adaptive nav, sticky action dock, and on-demand Chip sheet/panel with no permanent content reservation.
modules: App.tsx, app-shell.css, ChipDock.tsx, MobileBottomTabBar.tsx, overlay layout
acceptance: Phone global chrome including safe-area treatment stays within a defined 152 px envelope; no content is permanently padded for expanded Chip; no occlusion at matrix viewports.

title: Small type, undersized targets, and equal visual intensity undermine usability
evidence: At 320×568 Briefing contains 270 small-text elements and 15 controls below 44 px; at 844×390, 48 of 49 interactive elements are below 44 px. The source contains 80 pixel-font references and extensive bright borders.
root: Retro identity tokens expanded into body/data roles; desktop controls were optimized for compactness; borders and accents carry too many semantic jobs.
impact: Scanning is slow, touch accuracy drops, and primary decisions do not stand out from labels and decoration.
affected: Small phones, landscape, large-text users, low-vision users, and coarse pointers.
direction: Readable sans body, tabular numeric face, selective condensed/display type, 48 px nominal targets, semantic color hierarchy, and strict accent budget.
acceptance: Phone body copy ≥16 px, essential labels ≥12 px, routine targets ≥44×44 (48 nominal), 200% zoom/reflow passes, and each screen has at most one primary accent plus one urgent signal.

title: New Dynasty is a six-screen-tall catalog before the player commits to a setup path
evidence: At 390×844 New Game is 5,055 px tall (6.0 viewports), with 56 interactive controls, 86 small-text elements, and 91 bordered elements; the Instant choice begins around y=3,484.
root: Franchise catalog, mode explanation, scenario options, and launch paths share one continuous page.
impact: The first decision feels like setup administration rather than starting a dynasty.
direction: Stage the flow: choose Start Type → choose franchise/search → choose experience → confirm. Preserve progress and allow instant/demo paths immediately.
acceptance: Every setup step fits within 1.5 phone viewports; primary path is visible in viewport one; back preserves selections.

title: App.tsx is a 2,229-line shell/controller/overlay/router concentration point
evidence: RootLayout owns shell rendering, navigation, keyboard behavior, lifecycle effects, command palette, tutorial, achievements, ceremonies, breaking news, playoff lore, recap, save reminder, and other overlays.
root: Cross-cutting UI responsibilities grew inside one root component.
impact: Every shell change has large regression radius; overlay ordering and responsive behavior are difficult to test independently.
direction: Split into MfdAppShell, route surface metadata, adaptive navigation, phase context, overlay provider, companion adapter, and lifecycle presenters.
acceptance: Root app composition becomes thin; shell/overlay/nav modules have isolated tests; no engine action moves into presentation code.

title: MondayBriefing.tsx mixes orchestration, layout, customization, copy, metrics, and task logic
evidence: 1,987 lines and multiple dashboard modes/widgets/pins/readiness explanations in one feature component.
root: No separation between derived weekly view model, task ledger, screen archetype, and optional modules.
impact: The most important screen is the hardest to safely simplify and test.
direction: Extract pure Today presenter and task ledger; compose bounded modules through a Today archetype.
acceptance: View model snapshot covers phases; screen component contains presentation composition, not business mutation logic.

title: Inline-style debt forces responsive CSS to fight specificity
evidence: 4,110 direct style object blocks across 199 TSX files; design tokens explicitly document data-attribute plus !important overrides because inline styles bypass responsive rules.
root: Screen-local styling bypasses semantic tokens and shared archetypes.
impact: Hierarchy changes are slow, inconsistent, and fragile across breakpoints.
direction: Introduce semantic tokens and scoped CSS Modules; migrate by route cluster, prohibit new layout-critical inline styles, and remove overrides only after replacement coverage.
modules: design-system tokens, screen CSS, lint/test rules
acceptance: New-shell surfaces contain no layout-critical inline styles; inline-style count decreases packet-by-packet with a tracked allowlist.

title: Desktop tables become kilometer-long bordered card stacks
evidence: Global mobile CSS turns table rows into flex-column cards and injects 8 px pixel labels for each cell; Roster reaches 11,802 px with 526 small-text and 358 bordered elements.
root: A single generic fallback replaces column-priority and task-specific mobile data design.
impact: Players lose cross-row comparison while scroll burden explodes.
affected: Roster, standings, contracts, draft, free agency, stats, records.
direction: Use purpose-specific mobile list rows, priority columns, horizontal comparison workbench only where justified, entity detail, filters, and virtualization thresholds.
acceptance: Each dense view documents mobile priorities; no generic all-cells-as-card fallback; Roster default phone length is bounded through grouping/filtering/virtualization.

title: One game is fragmented across globally separate destinations
evidence: Game Day, Broadcast, Presentation, Play-by-Play, Game Flow, Film Room, Schedule, and recap concepts are separate routes/groups.
root: Presentation modes were modeled as peers in global IA instead of states/tabs of a game entity.
impact: Postgame understanding requires route hopping and loses score/opponent context.
direction: Create Game Hub plus entity-based Game Center with Overview, Broadcast, Plays, Flow, Film, Box Score, and Consequences tabs; preserve old paths as aliases.
modules: game-day features, route registry, Game Center presenters
acceptance: From a game card, all game views retain the same game ID/context and switch locally; back returns to originating schedule/Today task.

title: Personnel acquisition is split across too many global routes
evidence: Trades, block, deadline, team needs, scouting, draft, recap, free agency, targets, waivers, practice squad, and camp are independently surfaced.
root: Lifecycle-specific tools lack a parent Personnel workspace and phase-aware entry points.
impact: Players must reconstruct a roster-building workflow from destination names.
direction: Office → Personnel with phase-aware tabs and transaction workbenches; surface the relevant stage on Today.
acceptance: Deadline and offseason fixture journeys can be completed from one workspace with preserved filters, selections, and backtracking.

title: News, Newsroom, Social, Pulse, Rankings, Standings, Stats, Records, and Analytics overlap without a clear question model
evidence: 13 league-room routes plus league content duplicated in ticker, Briefing, and other screens.
root: Content channels and analytical questions are mixed as global destinations.
impact: Players cannot predict where to answer “what happened,” “who is best,” or “why.”
direction: League hub with Overview, Race, News, Stats, Records, and Rules; embed contextual league snippets on team/player/game pages.
acceptance: Each league question has one canonical surface; duplicate summaries deep-link to that source rather than reproducing full modules.

title: Legacy value is buried in a 23-route archive taxonomy
evidence: Franchise, career, book, chronicle, scrapbook, legends, HOF, trophy room, eras, MVPs, lore, achievements, named games, bloodlines, awards, recap, and scenarios are separated.
root: Emotional artifacts were organized by feature implementation rather than story and moment.
impact: The deepest emotional payoff is discoverable mainly by menu browsing after the moment has passed.
direction: Dynasty hub organized as Story, People, Honors, Seasons, and Records; trigger relevant legacy moments after games, seasons, records, and milestones.
acceptance: Every legacy route maps to a hub section/detail; milestone fixtures provide an event entry and preserve old deep links.

title: GM Mode and Nerd Mode create two mental maps instead of one scalable system
evidence: Five room navigation coexists with eight alternate groups covering overlapping routes.
root: Expert density was solved by reorganizing navigation rather than progressively disclosing data.
impact: Learning one mode does not reliably transfer to the other.
direction: One IA; Comfortable and Compact density preferences, advanced sections, saved views, comparison, and command search serve experts.
acceptance: Mode removal does not hide any route; compact changes density, not location or labels.

title: Borders, badges, and accent colors make too many elements appear primary
evidence: Briefing has 156 bordered elements at 320×568; More has 230; Roster phone has 358. Screens use multiple bright semantic and decorative border colors.
root: Panels are the default container and accent color performs branding, status, navigation, and hierarchy simultaneously.
impact: Focal points disappear; the UI feels noisy and less premium.
direction: Plain sections by default, three neutral surface levels, borders only for grouping/state, strict accent budget, whitespace and type for hierarchy.
acceptance: Visual-emphasis audit shows one primary action and at most one urgent competing signal per screen; decorative border count materially drops.

title: Pixel typography and uppercase microcopy are used beyond brand moments
evidence: 80 pixel typography references and 52 uppercase transforms; phone runtime includes hundreds of visible elements below 12 px.
root: Retro broadcast identity is implemented as a pervasive text system.
impact: Dense football information becomes harder to scan, especially at mobile distance.
direction: Use readable sans for body, condensed display for headings, tabular mono for data; reserve pixel face for logo, short kicker, and rare broadcast moments.
acceptance: No paragraph/table cell/form label uses pixel type; essential copy meets minimum sizes and 200% zoom.

title: Nested scroll and inconsistent route restoration obscure where the player is
evidence: Phone shell commonly reports three scroll containers; some route documents appear short because content lives in a nested main region. Global header, main, drawers, and overlays can each scroll.
root: Shell and screens independently own overflow without a single archetype contract.
impact: Back, focus restoration, and scroll restoration are unpredictable; users can feel trapped inside long data views.
direction: One primary scroll region per archetype; explicit local scrollers for tables only; route-state restoration keyed by entity/task origin.
acceptance: No unexplained nested scroll; route tests assert scroll/focus/back behavior; drawers trap and restore focus correctly.

title: Chip’s valuable guidance is coupled to a large persistent footprint and duplicate task messaging
evidence: Shell reserves 320 px bottom or 310–370 px right when Chip is active; Chip repeats pending-decision and location guidance also present elsewhere.
root: The companion is implemented as a persistent dock rather than a presentation adapter over canonical context.
impact: Players may minimize useful guidance just to reclaim space, while those who keep it open receive redundant signals.
direction: 44–48 px trigger; mobile bottom sheet; desktop on-demand side panel; same Task Ledger and route context; speak at blockers, consequences, onboarding, and major moments.
acceptance: No permanent layout reservation; minimize/mute/reopen works; Chip and Today task fixtures always agree.

title: Settings/save/help are long feature pages rather than calm trust-critical utilities
evidence: Settings phone capture is 8,548 px (10.1 viewports); save/load and backup behavior are spread among utility surfaces and cartridge concepts.
root: System options accumulated in the same panel-heavy screen pattern as game systems.
impact: Users have difficulty finding recovery, accessibility, import/export, and reversible settings when confidence matters most.
affected: Returning users, failures, device migration, accessibility setup.
direction: System sheet plus dedicated Save & Recovery and Settings surfaces grouped by task, with status, last-save proof, and safe staged actions.
acceptance: Autosave status and recovery are visible; export/import flows explain scope and preserve compatibility; settings categories are searchable and keyboard/touch complete.

title: External font dependence can weaken offline visual consistency
evidence: Runtime capture aborted external requests and rendered fallback fonts; product is browser-first and local-first.
root: Brand typography can rely on network availability.
impact: Offline or restricted networks may shift metrics and hierarchy.
direction: System-first body stack and locally bundled selective display assets only if measured against bundle gate.
acceptance: Core layout remains stable with network blocked; no essential UI depends on third-party font fetch.

title: Global overlays lack a visible orchestration contract
evidence: RootLayout mounts tutorial, achievements, ceremonies, breaking news, halftime, hotkeys, playoff lore, recap, era prompt, and save reminder.
root: Each overlay independently competes for timing and layer priority.
impact: Rare states can stack, steal focus, or interrupt another critical workflow.
direction: Central overlay queue with priority, exclusivity, preemption, dedupe, persistence, and focus rules.
acceptance: Synthetic collision tests produce deterministic ordering and one blocking overlay at a time.

title: Command Deck is visually prominent enough to feel required
evidence: CTRL+K and command affordances appear in global chrome near core navigation.
root: Search compensates for route complexity.
impact: New players may believe they need to know names before finding features.
direction: Keep command search as a power tool; hubs and contextual links must complete core journeys without it.
acceptance: Core playtest never invokes search; search remains reachable and improves expert speed.

title: Locked and phase-specific features need consistent explanation
evidence: Routes include unlock week/phase metadata, but presentation varies across navigation and screens.
root: Availability is expressed per feature rather than through a shared unavailable-state component.
impact: Players cannot distinguish “not yet,” “wrong phase,” and “missing prerequisite.”
direction: Shared AvailabilityState with reason, unlock condition, preview, and relevant next action.
acceptance: All locked route fixtures render reason and path forward; no dead-end disabled controls.

title: Empty/loading/error states are not governed by a shared archetype contract
evidence: Large feature surface area and local screen implementations imply inconsistent handling; direct runtime did not traverse every exceptional state.
root: No design-system state pattern or route-level test matrix.
impact: Failures or empty seasons can feel like broken screens.
affected: Imports, empty lists, phase transitions, async-like operations.
direction: Shared state frame with title, explanation, recovery, diagnostics ID, and preserved context.
acceptance: Every migrated route has loading/empty/error/locked test cases or an explicit not-applicable record.

title: No unified density contract separates comfort from expert throughput
evidence: Current GM/Nerd split changes navigation while many screens remain independently dense.
root: Density is encoded in individual styles and routes.
impact: Experts cannot reliably compact data without changing mental model; novices still see advanced noise.
direction: Comfortable/Compact tokenized density; mobile defaults comfortable; advanced sections and saved views persist in UI preferences.
acceptance: Density changes spacing/row height only, not information location or route availability.

title: Player/team/game links do not share a consistent origin and return model
evidence: Many global routes link into related objects, but current route taxonomy is screen-centered rather than entity-centered.
root: Navigation helpers lack explicit origin/task context.
impact: Drill-down interrupts the workflow and back may return to an unexpected surface.
affected: Roster comparison, game review, transactions, league stats.
direction: Typed entity links and return context: origin route, tab, filter, scroll key, and active task.
acceptance: Entity drill-down fixture returns to preserved filter/selection/scroll after Back or “Return to task.”

title: Short-height layouts remain technically operable but vertically inefficient
evidence: Briefing reaches 8,059 px at 667×375 (21.5 viewports) and 7,449 px at 844×390 (19.1 viewports).
root: Responsive rules focus on width while global chrome and stacked modules ignore height.
impact: Landscape is worse, not better, for management screens.
direction: Compact-height shell, horizontal context/actions, collapsed optional modules, and game-presentation-specific landscape layout.
acceptance: 375–430 px height matrix keeps primary action visible, no occlusion, and uses compact-height tokens.

title: No durable visual/measurement baseline appears integrated into release gates
evidence: Audit required custom capture scripts; existing release gate lists many checks but retained artifact does not show route/viewport visual baselines.
root: Functional coverage matured faster than UI regression infrastructure.
impact: A shell rewrite could silently reintroduce overflow, buried actions, or target-size failures.
direction: Add deterministic fixture capture, geometry assertions, axe checks, and approved visual baselines for archetypes.
acceptance: Critical route/viewport matrix runs in CI or release gate with diff thresholds and geometry assertions.

title: Tiny badges and count affordances can lack sufficient semantic weight
evidence: Global navigation and Chip use compact count treatments amid dense chrome.
root: Badges are used for both status and urgency.
impact: Counts can be missed or overinterpreted.
direction: Standard badge variants with text alternatives, capped counts, and urgency semantics.
acceptance: Badges are never the only cue and have accessible names.

title: Icon and label patterns are inconsistent across dense controls
evidence: Current UI mixes text-only, abbreviated, symbolic, and command-style controls.
root: Feature-local controls evolved without one interaction grammar.
impact: Recognition and touch confidence decrease.
direction: Labeled icons only when the symbol is conventional; consistent verb-first action copy.
acceptance: Component inventory documents icon/label behavior and automated accessible names.

title: Internal taxonomy, abbreviations, and all-caps copy can obscure plain football meaning
evidence: Runtime includes labels such as GM MODE, CMD DECK, source/debug-like descriptions, and extensive uppercase styling.
root: Developer/system language leaks into player-facing hierarchy.
impact: Players spend attention decoding the interface.
direction: Plain-language copy system: action, reason, consequence; move provenance/debug detail behind Help/Details.
acceptance: Content review removes unexplained internal terms from primary flows.

title: Border/elevation values are duplicated instead of semantically constrained
evidence: Large bordered-element counts and screen-local styling imply many local combinations.
root: No strict semantic surface/border hierarchy.
impact: Polish drifts across route clusters.
direction: Three surface levels, three border roles, two elevation levels, and one overlay layer family.
acceptance: New UI uses semantic tokens; lint/style review rejects raw repeated values outside tokens.
